To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The high-frequency ultrasonic phased array device can be realized with a high efficiency, 2) The device has a high directivity and a good focusing ability, and 3) The device has good electrical performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, fabrication and characterization of a high frequency ultrasonic transducer array.
the design and optimization of high-frequency (>50 MHz) ultrasonic transducer array for medical imaging.
the feasibility of high frequency (>100 MHz) linear array transducer based on MEMS technologies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the high-frequency (>100MHz) ultrasonic phased arrays are feasible using MEMS technologies.
it is feasible to design and fabricate a high frequency ultrasonic transducer with a high resolution using MEMS technologies.
the design of high frequency (>100 MHz) linear phased array transducer using MEMS technologies is possible and the performance is acceptable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the design of the MEMS LiNbO3 phased array transducer is feasible.
, with the proper design, the proposed device could be a potential candidate for high frequency ultrasonic imaging.
it is possible to design and fabricate high frequency ultrasonic array transducer with a wide frequency range, good beam steering and focusing performance, and low cross-talking.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the high frequency ultrasonic array transducer can be realized using MEMS technology and that the beam performance is very sensitive to the array matching conditions.
the high frequency ultrasonic array transducer can be designed and fabricated using MEMS technologies and can be used for medical imaging applications.
it is possible to design and simulate high-frequency (>100MHz) ultrasonic phased arrays using MEMS technologies.
